summary.name: multiprocessing
summary.one_liner: Python standard library package for process-based parallelism, spawning subprocesses with an API similar to the threading module.
use_cases: Parallelizing a function across many input values
Using multiple CPU cores from Python
Sharing data between processes via queues or pipes
Synchronizing output between processes with locks
summary.what_it_does: The module spawns processes using an API similar to threading, side-stepping the GIL by using subprocesses instead of threads. It provides a Process class (start, join, terminate, kill, interrupt, exitcode, daemon) and a Pool class for distributing function calls over input data. It offers Queue and Pipe for message passing between processes, and locks and other synchronization primitives equivalent to those in threading. It supports three start methods (spawn, fork, forkserver) selectable via set_start_method or get_context.
notable: Pool object for data parallelism with map, imap_unordered, and apply_async
Multiple start methods: spawn, fork, forkserver, with context objects
Process API that mirrors threading.Thread, plus terminate, kill and interrupt
caveats: Not supported on Android, iOS, WASI or WebAssembly platforms
spawn and forkserver start methods generally cannot be used with frozen executables (PyInstaller, cx_Freeze) on POSIX
Code using Pool or Process needs an importable __main__ module, so examples may fail in the interactive interpreter
